public_rationale: Marcus warns that agent deployment is dangerous unless safety improves substantially. He does not give a measurable safety condition or a specific accident forecast. The research and later incident report inform that concern, but cannot turn it into a binary test. Calling the warning supported because an incident occurred would impose the same firm-forecast reading that the reviewers rejected.
limitations: This decision concerns whether the wording can be scored, not whether agent deployment poses serious risks.
The incident evidence is company-reported and is not an exhaustive record of deployed agents.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Unless safety practices radically improve, deploying LLMs as agents will lead to accidents.
conditions: unless we radically up our game

statement.excerpt: Unless we radically up our game, deploying LLMs as agents is an accident waiting to happen.
statement.document_title: LLMs: Dishonest, unpredictable and potentially dangerous.

from_speaker: Unless we radically up our game
our_interpretation: This is a conditional warning about unsafe deployment. The idiom does not specify an accident, its severity, its likelihood, or when it will occur.
The antecedent would be the absence of a radical improvement in safety practices, not the occurrence of such an improvement.
The surrounding discussion points to autonomous operation, sensitive information, and limited human oversight. It supplies no threshold for deciding whether safety practices have improved radically.
Turning this warning into a firm prediction that any subsequent agent incident would verify would add commitments the speaker did not make.
criteria.support_condition: No binary support test can be specified faithfully from these words alone. Relevant incidents can substantiate the concern, but cannot establish the undefined safety antecedent or verify a specified forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No binary contradiction test can be specified faithfully. An incident-free interval cannot refute an undated risk warning, and improvements cannot be classified as radical without an added standard.

evidence.excerpt: We have not seen evidence of agentic misalignment in real deployments.
evidence.explanation: Anthropic distinguished its simulated failures from observed deployment incidents at publication. This neither disproves a future risk nor establishes Marcus's safety antecedent.

evidence.locator: Introduction, paragraph beginning 'The cases we’ve identified'
evidence.explanation: This is Anthropic's dated assessment of incidents observed during evaluations and internal use. The report also describes remedial safeguards, but neither incidents nor remediation determine what Marcus meant by radical improvement.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A clarified claim specifying the safety condition, deployment scope, qualifying harm, likelihood, and time period could be assessed prospectively. Those criteria should not be invented after observing incidents.
